content.comment_body: Hello everyone, my name is [user_name] and I'm new to this forum. Some time ago, I purchased two [product_name] controllers (type [article_no]) with both analog and digital expansion modules, along with an operator panel for managing my heating system. I'm mostly self-taught when it comes to [company_name] devices, so I might lack some technical knowledge in specific areas. For my first controller, I used two digital expansion modules ([article_no]), one larger digital module ([article_no]), and three analog modules ([article_no]) to implement the thermal management functions: - Pellet replenishment to the fireplace via auger from an auxiliary tank - Controlling pumps, connected simply with in-out digital signals (no modbus, knx, etc.) - Managing tank water stratification and controlling the fireplace operation - Regulating the supply water temperature with a climate curve With the second controller and another digital module ([article_no]), I set up anomaly detection: - Pump malfunction alerts - Primary pump anomaly for the fireplace - Pellet tank empty notification The operator device in the living room is used for complete system monitoring. Everything works well overall, except for one issue: both controllers sometimes unexpectedly switch from RUN to STOP mode, halting all operations. This can happen intermittently—for instance, one may run for several days before stopping, while the other could stop multiple times in a single day. Does anyone have insights on what could cause this? The problem seems to happen independently across the two units. Thank you very much to all who can offer advice, [user_name].
Hello [user_name], Welcome to the forum. Please note this is an English-speaking community, so kindly submit future posts in English. Thank you.

Which [product_name] ([article_no]) do you have, and what is the exact firmware version? If it's a [product_name] with display and firmware version [version_no], there is a known firmware issue that cannot be repaired.

Hello [user_name], Welcome to the [company_name] forum. Since the community is global, we've adopted English as the standard language for clarity. Please write in English or use a translator for future posts (I'm currently using Google Translate). I suggest you zip and attach your program files so experienced members can review and provide advice. Hope that helps, [user_name] Translation of the Italian message thanks to Google Translate:

Hi [user_name], As mentioned, please upload your project file (in zip format) so members can help check for possible errors in your setup. In some cases, the problem may be due to a known firmware issue in one version of the [product_name] controller, which caused unexpected STOP events—updating the firmware resolved the issue in my case.

There was only a single [product_name] version that showed the unexpected switch from RUN to STOP: the [product_name] type [version_no] with firmware [version_no]. Firmware updates are not possible for this model, so the error cannot be fixed. Also, errors in the user program cannot cause the controller to switch to STOP.

@ [user_name], It's rare for me to disagree with you, but regarding firmware [version_no], one of its fixes was related to network communication between the controller and operator panel when used over long periods, mostly affecting setups running for more than 50 days. After updating the firmware in my case, I had no issues after 2018. Since we haven't reviewed the user's program yet, we can't determine the exact cause. Let's wait for them to upload the project.

I also have to disagree with that statement. The 50-day issue actually affected controllers of the second generation with firmware versions [version_no]. According to product documentation for [product_name] ([article_no], [version_no]), this problem was unrelated to the automatic switch to STOP. The unexpected switch to STOP applied to first-generation controllers with firmware [version_no], which were not updatable and thus could not be repaired.

Hi, Another possible cause is an unstable power supply. If the power source fluctuates, the [product_name] may enter STOP mode instead of continuing in RUN. When a power drop occurs during the boot sequence, if the minimum voltage requirement isn't met, the controller may start up in STOP mode. This can happen even after a return of power, depending on timing and conditions. Hope this helps.
Good morning and thank you all for your responses. I am sending my project for you to analyze. Have a great day!
No user program error can cause a [product_name] controller to switch itself to STOP mode. Therefore, please specify precisely which [product_name] you have (full order number and firmware version).
That's exactly what I said. These controllers with firmware [version_no] cannot be repaired. If you're unsure, contact [company_name] directly by submitting a support request.

Thank you very much for all the advice. I've found similar reports about this firmware and version on the [company_name] forums, which confirms what you've said. Much appreciated, have a good day to you and the whole forum.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are reporting that their [product_name] controllers randomly switch from RUN to STOP mode, interrupting automation. The issue is unpredictable and difficult to diagnose, with discussions centered around whether the cause is a firmware defect, instability in the power supply, or unrelated to the user program. This uncertainty undermines confidence in the reliability of these devices.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] controllers to operate reliably and without unexpected interruptions. They look for stable system performance and clear diagnostics to identify any faults quickly.
